about.title: Murrieta Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Murrieta is a driving city. School runs move along Clinton Keith Road, shopping trips cluster on Murrieta Hot Springs Road, and commutes funnel through Winchester Road and Whitewood Road. Riverside County public records for 2025 list 426 injury collisions inside the city, with 595 people hurt and 7 lives lost. Reports tend to cluster on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., when traffic builds ahead of the weekend. If one of those numbers is you or someone in your family, the practical questions arrive fast: who pays for the ER visit, how do you replace the car, and what should you say to the other driver's insurer. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Murrieta residents with an independent personal injury attorney who takes car accident cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. California allows two years to file in most cases, but dashcam footage, witness contacts, and vehicle damage disappear much sooner, which is why an early conversation helps.

items.title: You Won't Miss a Deadline
items.desc: California's statute of limitations is generally two years for a car accident, but claims involving a city, county, or state agency can require notice in as little as six months. The attorney we connect you with will pin down which clock applies to your crash.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you shared some blame for a collision on Winchester Road, you can still recover damages reduced by your percentage. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your share.

items.title: Nothing Owed Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, and our connection service is free. California also places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost quality of life in ordinary car accident cases, so your full harm can be considered.

items.question: The other driver's insurer keeps calling about my Murrieta crash. Should I give a recorded statement?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement, and it is usually wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used later to reduce or deny your claim. Instead, gather your photos, the police report number from Murrieta PD or CHP, and any witness contacts, and let an attorney handle the communication.

items.question: What if the crash happened at a poorly maintained intersection on Whitewood Road or another city street?
items.answer: If a road defect or missing signal contributed to the collision, part of your claim may be against the City of Murrieta, Riverside County, or Caltrans. Claims against government entities in California typically must be filed within six months, far shorter than the usual two years. That is a strong reason to get an attorney reviewing your case quickly rather than waiting.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident lawsuit in California?
items.answer: For most car accident injury claims, California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. Property damage claims have a three-year window, and claims involving a public agency have much shorter notice requirements. Even with two years available, the strongest cases are usually built in the first few weeks while evidence is fresh.
